title: Family planning demand satisfied (modern methods), LDCs, LLDCs and SIDS compared with the World
custodian: UN DESA Population Division and UNFPA
headline: Demand met with modern methods since 2000: 21.6 points in LDCs, 20.8 in LLDCs, 1.5 in SIDS
subtitle: Demand for family planning satisfied with modern methods - percentage of women (aged 15-49 years)
years: LDCs: from 38.5% in 2000 to 60.1% in 2025. World: from 73.7% to 77.2%.
data_line: Data: UN DESA Population Division and UNFPA via UN SDG Global Database, series SH_FPL_MTMM, extracted 1 Nov 2026
alt: Demand met with modern methods since 2000: 21.6 points in LDCs, 20.8 in LLDCs, 1.5 in SIDS. LDCs: from 38.5% in 2000 to 60.1% in 2025. World: from 73.7% to 77.2%. LDCs: 38.5% in 2000 to 60.1% in 2025; LLDCs: 43.7% in 2000 to 64.5% in 2025; SIDS: 67.2% in 2000 to 68.7% in 2025; World: 73.7% in 2000 to 77.2% in 2025
question: What lies behind the change in demand met with modern methods in Least developed countries, and what could others learn from it?
